content:
Daily scratchpad - account reminders and quick to-dos
Date: 2026-07-15
Owner: Isabel Hart
Context: ramping QBR prep for ACME Corp (renewal window Aug 10), several ongoing support tickets that need follow-ups before the QBR to avoid surprises. Quick personal checklist and notes to pull into QBR deck.

Top priorities (today):
1) ACME QBR prep: finalize agenda + risks slide
   - Draft agenda: 1) Wins & adoption metrics, 2) Performance/cost review, 3) Support incidents & mitigations, 4) Roadmap + feature asks, 5) Renewal/contract discussion
   - Needs: updated latency/cost chart from observability team (ask Ryan). Deadline: EOD 2026-07-16 for internal review.
   - Action: email Ryan Cole now for figures and confirm export format (CSV + PNG).

2) Renewal follow-up: ACME (renewal target Aug 10)
   - Renewal owner: Sales (Maya). Current ask: 20% discount request; legal needs T&Cs.
   - My role: prepare usage justification (savings by moving to Dedicated), propose two options (12-month commit w/ lower price vs 6-month w/ smaller discount).
   - Action items: pull 6-month token usage by route (hosted API) - ping infra/observability for per-route breakdown (ticket JIRA CS-4521).

3) Support follow-ups before QBR (do these this morning):
   - TICKET CS-4478 (schema mismatch after model upgrade) - assigned to DevEng, owner Jordan. Status: in-progress, ETA 7/16. Need postmortem bullet for QBR. ACTION: request root-cause summary + mitigation plan by 7/16.
   - TICKET CS-4502 (embedding drift) - assigned to Applied ML. Status: investigating. Ask for short explanation of drift and proposed evaluation set for QBR demo.
   - TICKET CS-4539 (SAML login flakiness for two users) - SRE to confirm fix deployed; verify with customer. ACTION: schedule quick 15m with customer if SRE confirms.

Meeting/communication schedule:
- 10:00 AM - Sync with Jordan (30m) to get summaries for support tickets + postmortem bullets.
- 11:30 AM - Call with ACME CSM (prep call w/ Sales & Legal reps) - confirm renewal timeline and any open procurement blockers.
- 2:00 PM - Internal QBR content review (product + observability) - need draft deck by 1:30 PM.

Draft QBR talking points (bullets to refine):
- Adoption: 3x increase in prompt throughput last quarter, top 5 routes: search, summarization, chat-assist, ingestion pipeline, analytics.
- Performance: median p95 latency 220ms on Hosted API, Dedicated nodes reduced cost per token by ~18% for heavy batch workloads.
- Reliability: three incidents last quarter; two were customer-side (schema + auth), one was infra-related (KV cache eviction) - mitigation and safeguards now in place (cache TTL tuning, canary deploys).
- Cost optimization: proposal to enable prefix caching + intelligent batching for ACME's top-heavy routes - estimated savings: $8k/month.
- Roadmap ask: prioritized request is fine-grained routing policy for region-specific fallbacks (Engineering roadmap Q4).

Notes / quick facts to include in deck:
- Renewal date: Aug 10, 2026
- Current ARR: $180k/year (confirm with Sales)
- Primary contacts at ACME: Samantha Lee (Head of AI), Raj Patel (Platform lead) - get updated emails from Sales.
- Most used model variants: redwood-instruct-3b (hosted), quantized-4bit for Dedicated pools.

Risks & escalations:
- If analytics team can't produce per-route cost by EOD 7/16, we won't have the optimization slide for the customer - escalate to Ryan.
- Legal turnaround on discount terms could take 7-10 business days - flag with Sales to get early heads-up.

To-do list (prioritized):
- [ ] Email Ryan Cole for latency/cost export (ASAP)
- [ ] Ping observability for per-route token usage (attach JIRA CS-4521)
- [ ] Request ticket summaries and postmortem bullets from Jordan (before 10am sync)
- [ ] Draft QBR deck skeleton and share with Maya + Jordan by 1:30 PM
- [ ] Confirm SRE fix and, if deployed, arrange verification call with ACME for 7/16
- [ ] Compile proposed renewal options for Sales (2 options doc)
- [ ] Add speaker notes for "Cost optimization" slide with estimated numbers

Scratch notes / things to remember:
- Put a short appendix with "how to interpret latency/cost graph" - customers like the quick ROI calc (tokens -> $).
- Keep technical details high-level in slides; deep-dive appendices for interested engineers.
- Bring examples of embeddings regression and the evaluation harness we ran (applied-ml artifact link).

Quick messages to send (copy templates):
- To Ryan: "Ryan - can you export per-route token counts + cost breakdown for ACME for the last 6 months? Need CSV + PNG for QBR. Target: EOD 7/16. JIRA CS-4521 attached for context. Thanks - Isabel."
- To Jordan: "Jordan - can you prepare a short RCA + mitigation bullets for CS-4478 and confirm ETA? I'll include a short postmortem slide in the QBR. 10am sync."

End-of-day goals:
- Internal deck submitted for review; at least one support incident postmortem ready; renewal options drafted and shared with Sales.

Quick log (timeboxed):
- 08:30 - triage tickets; sent Ryan + Jordan messages
- 09:00 - follow-up with observability (no response yet)
- 09:45 - prep for 10:00 sync with Jordan

Notes to self: keep the QBR deck <15 slides; include two appendices (incidents + technical deep-dive). Use the customer success QBR template and populate numbers not more than 2 hours before meeting to ensure freshness.

---
End scratchpad.
